newsitem.title: UK: Major sees voters moving to Tories in coming weeks.
newsitem.headline: Major sees voters moving to Tories in coming weeks.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Friday he was disappointed by his Conservative Party's performance in the Wirral South by-election, but remained confident of victory at the forthcoming general election.

In a statement issued after the Conservatives lost the previously safe seat by 7,888 votes, Major said in a statement: "Of course I'm disappointed by the result-- it's a poor reward for an excellent candidate," Major said.
"But last night's result won't affect people's lives. The by-election is the end of the phoney war. Next time, a cross in the wrong box could mean Britain takes a wrong turning."
He said he did not believe that at the general election, people would elect a Labour party that would raise spending, taxes and interest rates.

"But that's what will happen if they vote in a Labour government - and very quickly. It will grow increasingly clear to the electorate over the coming weeks, and that is why at the general election we will win." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
